name: Luvale
notes: Standard Chiluvale (Luvale) Latin orthography, standardized by Zambia's Ministry of Education in 1977 alongside Bemba, Nyanja, Tonga, Lozi, Kaonde and Lunda (the seven official Zambian regional languages; Luvale is also the recognized national/trade language of Zambia's North-Western Province, shared with communities in Angola and the DR Congo). Five underlying vowel phonemes /a e i o u/ (each with phonemic length, written by doubling the vowel letter — AGENTS.md test 2, the same geminate-vowel pattern as cab.json) with the open-mid vowels [ɛ] [ɔ] as contextual allophones of /e/ /o/, retained here from the cited PHOIBLE-sourced inventory rather than re-analysed as separate phonemes. ⟨ch⟩ spells the affricate /t̠ʃ/ and ⟨nj⟩ its prenasalized counterpart /n̠d̠ʒ/, ⟨mb⟩/⟨nd⟩/⟨ng⟩ the prenasalized stops /mb/ /nd/ /ŋɡ/ — each a single unit segment, not a nasal followed by an oral obstruent (the prenasalized-stop pattern documented for Tiv). ⟨ng'⟩ (with a following apostrophe) spells the plain velar nasal /ŋ/, the same disambiguating convention documented for Zambian Tonga, Lozi and Lunda under the shared 1977 harmonized orthography (AGENTS.md test 3). ⟨ny⟩ is the palatal nasal /ɲ/, ⟨l⟩ the lateral flap /ɺ/, ⟨v⟩ the labiodental approximant /ʋ/. Most Luvale verb infinitives begin with the ⟨ku-⟩ prefix; smoke-tested against the cited example ⟨kutonga⟩ [kutoŋɡa] 'to sew' (the k-u-t-o-ŋɡ-a segments all resolve through the mapped graphemes above, ⟨ng⟩ correctly read as the prenasalized stop rather than n+g) and the cited Portuguese loanword ⟨xikata⟩ (from escada) 'ladder', whose non-native ⟨x⟩ onset is outside the native consonant inventory and is not modelled (a loanword gap, not a spec error). Luvale is a four-tone language with no lexical word stress; tone is not consistently marked in ordinary orthography and is left unencoded here, a documented exemption distinct from stress (docs/quality_tiers.md).
